close_reason: Rustdoc 'Properties' section added covering None/Some(&[])/Some(&[..]) semantics, RFC 8620 §5.1 silent-ignore for unknown names, and the cross-backend stability expectation. Handler at event.rs:1029-1067 already implements this contract; this commit just publishes it on the trait surface.
description:
crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/backend.rs:521-542 defines:

    fn parse_calendar_event_blobs(
        &self,
        _caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
        _account_id: &Id,
        blob_ids: &[Id],
        _properties: Option<&[String]>,
    ) -> impl ... -> Result<ParseResult, Self::Error>

Note `_properties` is leading-underscore-named (ignored by the default impl). The rustdoc at :521-525 describes only blob ids and the default behavior — it says NOTHING about what `properties` does:

- Whether a backend implementing non-default behavior should produce CalendarEvent objects with only the requested properties populated (RFC 8620 §5.1-style projection).
- Whether passing `Some(&[])` means "no properties — just confirm parseability" or "default property set".
- Whether `None` means "default properties" or "all properties".
- Whether unknown property names are rejected, ignored, or surfaced via a separate ParseResult bucket.

Compare draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26 §5.13 (CalendarEvent/parse): the spec defines the `properties` argument and the behavior of restricting parsed objects to those properties. But the trait method's rustdoc does not relay this.

What callers cannot rely on:
- That two backend impls produce the same CalendarEvent shape when given the same `properties` argument.
- That the handler (event.rs:983-1003) does any post-processing — it does not; the result is forwarded verbatim.
- That `properties: Some(&["title"])` will produce `CalendarEvent` objects with ONLY `title` populated, vs full objects.

Fix: add to the rustdoc:

    The `properties` argument selects which CalendarEvent properties
    are populated in the `parsed` map (per RFC 8620 §5.1). Backends
    MUST honor this when implementing non-default behavior. `None` =
    return all properties (server-defined "default property set");
    `Some(&[])` = parse but return only the `id` and required keys;
    unknown property names MUST be silently ignored per RFC 8620 §5.1.

Without this, every non-default backend will make its own decisions and clients will see different responses against different deployments.
title: parse_calendar_event_blobs accepts properties arg with no documented effect; backends silently disagree
